name: Lopinavir/ritonavir
drug_class: HIV protease inhibitor, boosted with ritonavir (CYP3A inhibitor)
route_note: oral tablets, oral solution or pellets for children, once or twice daily

discovery.note: Lopinavir was designed with ritonavir boosting in mind, as it is almost entirely metabolised by CYP3A4 when given alone.

tagline: First co-formulated boosted protease inhibitor, long a second-line and paediatric mainstay
summary: Lopinavir/ritonavir combines the protease inhibitor lopinavir with low-dose ritonavir, which blocks CYP3A4 and raises lopinavir levels. It was the first co-formulated boosted protease inhibitor and was long a standard second-line and paediatric HIV regimen in low-income countries. Trials in COVID-19 found no benefit.
mechanism: Lopinavir binds the active site of HIV-1 protease and blocks cleavage of the Gag-Pol polyprotein, so virus particles remain immature and non-infectious.

Ritonavir, itself a protease inhibitor, is used here at a low dose mainly to inhibit CYP3A4-mediated metabolism of lopinavir, raising its concentrations many-fold. This boosting also causes numerous drug interactions.
uses: HIV-1 infection in adults and children aged 14 days and older, in combination with other antiretrovirals

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Kaletra capsules and solution are approved in September 2000.

history.title: Tablet formulation
history.detail: A heat-stable melt-extrusion tablet is approved, removing the need for refrigeration.

history.title: Access pricing
history.detail: Abbott introduces the tablet as Aluvia at reduced prices for low-income countries; generic versions follow.

history.title: Paediatric pellets
history.detail: Oral pellets for young children receive FDA tentative approval, for use in low-resource settings.

history.title: COVID-19 trials
history.detail: Randomised trials including RECOVERY and WHO Solidarity show no benefit of lopinavir/ritonavir in hospitalised COVID-19.

pk.bioavailability: not established; solution taken with food

serious: toxicity of oral solution (ethanol and propylene glycol) in preterm neonates

facts: The oral solution contains about 42% ethanol and should not be used in premature babies.
Lopinavir was one of the earliest drugs repurposed and tested against COVID-19.

references.title: RECOVERY Collaborative Group. Lopinavir–ritonavir in patients admitted to hospital with COVID-19. Lancet 2020
